title: Regular-expression matching: backtracking vs memoised backtracking vs Thompson's NFA simulation
problem_statement: Dialect (defined here): a pattern is a sequence of atoms; an atom is a symbol, either a lowercase letter a-z (matches that letter) or '.' (matches any one character), optionally followed by one quantifier '?' (zero or one occurrence) or '*' (zero or more occurrences). No parentheses, alternation, character classes, anchors, escapes, lazy quantifiers or backreferences. Given a pattern with m atoms and a text t of length |t| over a-z, decide whether the WHOLE text matches the pattern (full match; Python's re.fullmatch semantics, of which this dialect is a subset).

input.parameter: n = size parameter: the pattern has at most 2n atoms (at most 4n characters) and the text at most 2n characters. The worst-case family is P_n = pattern (a?)^n a^n (m = 2n atoms) against text a^n (|t| = n).
input.size_measure: Theta(n) characters (pattern plus text). General bounds below are stated in m and |t|.

algorithms.name: backtracking (consume first)
algorithms.idea: Depth-first search over the choices, as in Perl-style engines: for 'c?' try consuming one character, then skipping the atom; for 'c*' try consuming and staying on the atom, then leaving it. Nothing is remembered between branches.
algorithms.pseudocode: match(i, j): if i == m: return j == |t|; (c, q) = atom i; ok = j < |t| and (c == '.' or c == t[j]); plain: ok and match(i+1, j+1); '?': (ok and match(i+1, j+1)) or match(i+1, j); '*': (ok and match(i, j+1)) or match(i+1, j). Answer match(0, 0).
algorithms.time_complexity: Exponential in the worst case. On P_n exactly (n + 2) * 2^(n-1) - 1 symbol-character comparisons, Theta(n * 2^n). In general O(2^(m + |t|)): every call makes at most two recursive calls and each increases i + j, so the call tree has depth <= m + |t| + 1.
algorithms.correctness: The recursion is the definition of full matching for a concatenation of atoms, explored exhaustively (an atom 'c?' matches the empty string or one character matching c; 'c*' matches the empty string or one character followed by a match of 'c*'). Count on P_n (proof): the n atoms 'a?' always can consume (j <= i < n), and the only accepting branch is 'skip all n', which consume-first explores last, so all 2^n branches of the first n atoms are explored, costing one comparison per internal node of the full binary tree: 2^n - 1. A branch that consumed j characters reaches the plain atoms with n - j characters left, compares n - j times and then fails at j = |t| without a comparison (or accepts if j = 0, after n comparisons). Total 2^n - 1 + sum_j C(n, j)(n - j) = 2^n - 1 + n 2^(n-1) = (n + 2) 2^(n-1) - 1.

algorithms.name: memoised backtracking
algorithms.idea: The same recursion with a table indexed by (atom index i, text position j): each of the at most (m + 1)(|t| + 1) subproblems is solved once.
algorithms.pseudocode: as backtracking, but match(i, j) first looks (i, j) up in a dictionary and stores its result
algorithms.time_complexity: O((m + 1)(|t| + 1)) subproblems with O(1) work each (O(1) dictionary operations, each counted as one step), i.e. O(n^2) for the stated n. On P_n exactly n(n + 1) symbol-character comparisons, Theta(n^2).
algorithms.correctness: Same recursion as backtracking; the result of match(i, j) depends only on (i, j), so caching it does not change the answer. Count on P_n (proof): one comparison per distinct visited state (i, j) with i < m and j < |t| whose atom is a letter; the visited states are (i, j) with 0 <= j <= i < n (n(n+1)/2 comparisons) and the chains (n + s, j + s) with j + s < n (another n(n+1)/2).

algorithms.name: Thompson's NFA simulation
algorithms.idea: Treat the atoms as NFA states 0..m and advance the SET of all states reachable after each text character in lock step: epsilon-closure (an optional atom can be skipped), then one transition per active state. No branch is ever revisited.
algorithms.pseudocode: S = closure({0}); for each character x of t: S = closure({i or i+1 : i in S, i < m, atom i matches x}); if S is empty: reject. Accept iff m in S. ('c*' stays at i, 'c' and 'c?' move to i + 1; closure follows optional atoms forward.)
algorithms.time_complexity: O(m (|t| + 1)): at most m + 1 states per step with O(1) work each, plus an O(m) closure per step; O(n^2) for the stated n. On P_n exactly n(n + 1) symbol-character comparisons, Theta(n^2).
algorithms.correctness: Thompson 1968. Invariant: after reading t[:j], S is exactly the set of atom positions i (0 <= i <= m) such that t[:j] fully matches atoms[:i] followed by c* when atom i is a starred atom c* (atoms[:i] alone otherwise); this set is closed under skipping optional atoms. Count on P_n (proof): the active set before reading character j + 1 is {j, ..., n + j} (n + 1 states, all < 2n), one comparison each, over n characters: n(n + 1).

relationship: Exponential -> polynomial on the same problem and inputs: on P_n, (n + 2) 2^(n-1) - 1 comparisons (backtracking) vs n(n + 1) (memoised backtracking and Thompson). The backtracking blow-up comes from re-exploring the same subproblem (i, j) along exponentially many branches; memoising the natural key (i, j) already gives a polynomial algorithm (RESEARCH_LOG RL-039 pattern), and Thompson's set simulation reaches the same bound without recursion or a table.

sources.title: Programming Techniques: Regular expression search algorithm

verification.method: V1: the three matchers agree with each other and with Python's re.fullmatch (an independent engine, used only as the oracle in harness.check) on seeded random instances for n = 0..12, 16, 20, 24, 6 trials each (backtracking up to n = 12); about a quarter of the instances for n <= 12 are the pathological P_n. A larger battery in experiments/2026-10-07b_regex_counts.py found 0 disagreements in 3300 instances (2275 matches). V2 (measure 'reported', RESEARCH_LOG RL-047 method): the measured quantity is the exact number of comparisons between a pattern symbol and a text character, counted by an instrumented character type (the text of P_n is built from it) while the matchers run unchanged. The counts equal the closed forms proved in this entry at every measured n (backtracking n = 0..16; memoised and Thompson n = 0..16, 24, 32, 48, 64). Fits: backtracking alpha = 0.974 against n*2^n at tolerance 0.035 (the 0.026 deviation is fixed by the exact lower-order terms of (n + 2) 2^(n-1) - 1; rivals 2^n 1.131, n^2*2^n 0.854, n^2 3.386, rejected; the log-factor diagnostic, 0.912 against n log n 2^n and 1.044 against n 2^n / log n, is resolved at this tolerance but was not at 0.06); memoised and Thompson alpha = 0.981 against n^2 at tolerance 0.05 (exact count n^2 + n; rivals n 1.962, n^3 0.654, n*2^n 0.058, rejected; log factor resolved: 0.852 and 1.156). Each tolerance exceeds the exact deviation and lies below every rival gap; see the validator output recorded in research/2026-10-07b_new_candidates.md.

caveats: The exponential cost of backtracking is family-specific: on most patterns it is fast, and P_n is one witness family (both pattern and text grow with n). Counts are symbol-character comparisons; loop control, the epsilon-closure and dictionary operations are not counted (they are O(1) per counted comparison or per state, so the asymptotic claims are unaffected). Backreferences are excluded: they can make the language non-regular and are handled by neither the NFA simulation nor this entry. Python's re is used only as the V1 oracle, never timed.
notes: Real backtracking engines add heuristics (and some memoise), but the consume-first depth-first strategy shown here is the classic source of 'catastrophic backtracking'. The memoised matcher and Thompson's simulation make the same number of comparisons on P_n, n(n + 1); they differ in that the simulation needs no table and reads the text strictly left to right once.
